Russian dance-pop is the dance-oriented subset of broader Russian pop, with overlap rather than categorical disjointness. Apple Music’s own artist curation positively calls Zivert dance-pop and categorizes her Essentials as Russian Pop. This differs in regional repertoire from the existing international 2010s EDM-pop umbrella and in stylistic subset from broad russian_pop, whose contemporary scope is explicitly acknowledged. Five named singers: Biguli,Fábio Allman,Momo,Pedro Luís,Pedro Quental. Three cavaquinho players: Alessandro,Cachaça,Carlinhos. Momo also guitar; Igor Araújo chocalho/bass. André Schmidt and Leo Saad agogô; C.A.Ferrari repique; Caco Chagas,Gabriel Lopes,Mário Moura,Maurão surdo; Celso Alvim,Fred Castilho,Gui Rodrigues,Marcos Feijão,Pitito caixa; Fábio Groove,Júnior Teixeira,Sidon Silva tamborim. Ten family cards preserve all26 credited human-role assignments and24 people, not ten performers. This is the documented standing group, not the expanded Carnaval student parade or an inferred individual recording session. Five credited voices do not establish simultaneous harmony voicing. Unspecified capture apparatus is omitted. tradition.lineage: De Braandheultjes — complete published eighteen-person carnival-association ensemble. The carnival association publishes the complete eighteen-person De Braandheultjes roster: eight trumpet players, two saxophonists, four trombonists, one sousaphonist and three percussionists. All five source families retained; no singers credited. Source explicitly calls the group a dweilorkest and describes carnival and other public appearances since1988. This models the whole published ensemble configuration, not a claimed audio transcription or a particular recorded set. No percussion object subtype is specified. Authored festive wind-and-percussion realization retains five positively credited families. Eight trumpeters, two saxophonists, four trombonists, one sousaphonist and three percussionists are represented by family cards rather than eighteen duplicate cards. B-flat Bach-style unmuted trumpet, alto Selmer-style saxophone, tenor Bach-style unmuted trombone and B-flat sousaphone are coherent editorial constructions, not measured source hardware or source-specified saxophone register. Punchy wind phrasing, honking saxophone accents, sectional trombone attacks and oom-pah sousaphone bass are authored party-band gestures, not a score transcription, a literal American big-band claim or proof every tune is a march. Source-unspecified percussion types stay neutral, without inventing drumkit or particular drum objects. No global temperament. Controlled live-room acoustic is an authored realization, not measured performance or capture equipment.

Complete Erratum Musical for three voices is the selected work, not Duchamps similarly named instrumental second Erratum or the whole mixed-program album. Edition Block separately lists this three-voice work in its S.E.M. Ensemble/Petr Kotik1991 release and distinguishes the Cage spoken mesostic, music-box version and other instrumental work. This authored performance follows the complete three-voice conception; no claim identifies the1991 individual singers or adds those other tracks instruments. Three authored singers each realize one positively scored voice part, represented by a single groupvoice card. Physiology/register/training remain unspecified. Neutral sung/spoken delivery and live group tracking preserve source-defined vocal parts without imposing conventional tonal harmony, sacred chant, numerical overdubs or exact original recording practices. Controlled concert-room acoustics are authored, capture hardware and global temperament omitted. tradition.name: Egyptian traditional
tradition.lineage: Muhammad El-Arabi — complete Darabukka solo, UNESCO UNES08038_106. Smithsonian Folkways issues Muhammad El-Arabi Darabukka solo as complete track6 UNES08038_106,3:58,1971, explicitly instrumental and credited only to El-Arabi on darabukka. Original UNESCO booklet identifies an earthenware single-skin drum and successive sama i thaqil10/8, darij3/4, nawakht7/8, aksak9/8, murabba13/4 and mukhammas16/8 rhythmic patterns, ending in a variation. No melodic instruments or singers from the other compilation tracks enter this complete solo scope. One clay darabukka preserves positively documented material and whole solo palette. Fish-skin membrane, Egyptian playing-school preset and open/slap hand technique are coherent authored traditional Egyptian choices; the source does not identify skin species, exact drum size or a Sombaty model. The existing Egyptian style label is an editorial regional realization, not an exact historical construction claim. Broad improvOnFrame follows the documented succession of rhythmic frames and final variation, not a melodic maqam imposed on an unpitched drum. Controlled live-room acoustic is authored, with unknown capture hardware and global tuning omitted. Rendered up-tempo wording is authored energetic solo affect, not a measured BPM claim about all source rhythmic sections.

extras.description: Adam Harper’s original2014 naming article identifies Epic Collage as a network and surreal narrative practice involving pop fragments, dramatic effects and cinematic textures; Total Freedom is explicitly one of its artists and its DJ-oriented branch. tradition.name: Er ge (Chinese children’s repertoire)
tradition.lineage: pichia — 小毛驢, complete four-page solo-piano theme and three variations. Arranger pichia publishes a complete four-page solo-piano adaptation of 小毛驢(Xiao Mao Lu/Little Donkey), including its theme and three variations labeled tango, Latin and waltz. Public arranger description explicitly calls the repertoire er ge/children song, specifies solo piano, printed lyrics and chords, C major and an Overture-generated listening example. Variations have no lyrics. Complete arrangement metadata was read; purchased full score and audio were not accessed. No original choir recording instrumentation is inferred from the piano edition. The selected published arrangement is explicitly piano solo despite printed lyrics; no singer is added. One nine-foot Steinway-D grand with conventional matching construction and block-chord song support is an authored physical realization, not the arranger playback piano model or source recording equipment. Broad functionalSong models the familiar song-theme and chordal dance variations, rather than treating notation alone as classical art music. Global tuning omitted; source C-major key is retained in evidence but does not prove a measured temperament. Studio capture choices are editorial.

Folk attribution is the arrangers own label, not an independently proven authorship/origin claim. The added tango/Latin/waltz variations belong to this adaptation; they do not redefine er ge as those genres. Global tuning omitted; source C-major key is retained in evidence but does not prove a measured temperament. Studio capture choices are editorial. Nearest existing mandarin_tongyao already spans mainland China, Taiwan, diaspora and regional Mandarin/Cantonese/other-Sinitic childhood play and rhyme corpora; no language or geographic exclusivity is claimed. Existing yaolanqu covers lullabies. This creator-defined Er Ge listening umbrella overlaps those practices but positively also includes narrated fairy tales/biographical stories (creator items20,29,30), standalone instrumental listening arrangements (item75 classical guitar and item1 music box), beyond a song/rhyme or lullaby-only definition. The selected Little Donkey piano edition is an adaptation of one shared repertoire item, not itself the boundary evidence.

tradition.name: Heligónka
tradition.lineage: Ladislav Bihari — Spievanky, spievanky, complete one-page heligónka arrangement issued by Miroslav Jurči / Pesničky pre všetkých. The specific score is for a two-row C/F instrument and retains the entire right-hand melody and harmonization, left-hand bass/chords, button choices and push/pull bellows directions. It is an authored instrumental realization of this complete instrumental arrangement, not a reconstruction of an unspecified vocal recording. Printed song lyrics and six verses remain source underlay/context; the publisher identifies the arrangement for heligónka, not a separate scored singer. No additional vocalist is inferred from printed words. The institutionally documented one-player heligónka practice supports this single-player realization; no claim all heligónka music is instrumental. Broad functionalSong represents the selected strophic folk-song melody and explicitly notated functional C/D-minor/F/G7 chord cycle, realized instrumentally across its verses. This does not imply Anglosphere pop/rock or through-composed concert art solely because a score exists. The isolated free-reed owner preserves four documented physical/playing dimensions: two C/F rows with eleven and ten right-hand buttons; a sixth-button F-row stoják retaining one pitch in both bellows directions; left-hand bass-plus-chord support; and explicitly scored push/pull melody phrasing. No manufacturer, reed metal, reed rank count, shell material or measured original tuning frequency is invented. Stoják-present option is selected from the score’s documented alternatives. Authored controlled live-room realization and equal-tempered baseline are editorial recording choices, not a source-session claim.

The arranger-issued product explicitly identifies solo piano for all ten hymns; her own profile identifies her as a Congregação Cristã no Brasil organist and hymn arranger. This is an instrumental realization of the complete published piano edition, with zero sung voices; it does not omit the voices or orchestra of a selected recording, claim every CCB service is instrumental, or reconstruct an unexamined video. Separate organ/keyboard adaptations are optional alternatives, not additional simultaneous instruments. The existing broad Christian sacred-song parent follows the explicitly CCB hymn purpose rather than treating notation alone as classical art music. A coherent nine-foot Steinway D, original felt hammers, maple rim/pinblock, spruce soundboard, iron plate and A440 are authored contemporary piano choices, not a claimed source instrument. Sustain-rich arpeggiated playing is an authored hymn realization, not a transcription of all ten scores. Controlled live-room acoustics are authored; no measured recording venue or capture hardware is asserted.

Editors who also read are counted once, and no additional musician is inferred from editorial coordination. The publisher explicitly tags this release hörspiel and its dramatic-work policy forbids added music and sound effects; this is a positively bounded voice-only dramatic reading branch, not an arbitrary reduction of a radio production with musical or foley credits. Fourteen is the reader count across the anthology, not14simultaneous singers, characters or recording tracks. Broad spokenWord is chosen because this selected edited digital dramatic reading is neither a single narrator, a live stand-up stage act nor an asserted broadcast session. The isolated spoken cast owner retains all17 original vocal physical/technique controls, with local spoken-ensemble and edited-dialogue options replacing sung choir and single-lead tracking assumptions. Fourteen credited readers are represented by one human-voice family card; individual physiology, actor-specific timbre, layering and recording locations remain unspecified. Pure spoken pitch treatment and a dry treated-studio acoustic realization are authored narration choices, not proof no character ever sings in the whole text or measured original booths. Source policy permits unaccompanied character singing where scripted; no such actual sung role is positively credited in this release, and the model does not assert an audio-forensic absence.

The issuer explicitly identifies the entire series as piano-solo scores and offers a companion piano-solo CD; this model selects the complete named arrangement, not an excerpt or a conjectured reduction of Frances Yip’s vocal soundtrack master. One piano performer, zero separately scored vocal parts. The TV broadcaster explicitly identifies Shanghai Bund among Koo’s television drama theme compositions. The instrumental arrangement retains the full selected edition; voices and orchestral roles from different recorded versions are not asserted or selectively omitted. Parent functionalSong.eastAsianPop retains the original Cantonese television-theme pop-song branch in its published instrumental realization. Merely owning a piano score does not turn this into artMusic or imply the entire category is instrumental. Coherent nine-foot Steinway D, original felt hammers, maple rim/pinblock, spruce board, iron plate and A440 are authored modern piano choices, not publisher recording equipment. tradition.name: Hüzünlü şarkılar
tradition.lineage: Kırık Pena — complete documented four-person concert ensemble established in 2023 and described by its concert ticketing provider: Yağızcan Yavuz drums, Furkan Durtaş vocals/guitar, Furkan Bulut electric guitar and Ekin Göre bass. Four people, one positively named singer, two guitarists represented by one electric-guitar family, bass and drum kit. The earlier first-person interview explicitly identifies Durtaş as vocalist/electric guitarist. This models the published performing quartet practice, not the differently produced 2020 Bulutlara Ağıt master: that earlier recording has positively documented piano and is not silently reduced to this lineup. The existing distortedRock.alternative parent reflects the provider explicit alternative-rock identity. A newly authored alder humbucker guitar with mahogany neck, ceramic pickups, power chords and standard tuning is paired with an alder electric bass, soapbar pickup, nickel roundwounds and picked articulation. Maple-shell stick-played drum kit with machine-hammered traditionally finished B20 cymbals is coherent authored rock scaffolding. These settings are not observed musician equipment. Neutral voice physiology is retained; small-note-groups-per-syllable singing is an authored treatment, not a source transcription. One credited vocalist does not establish actual recording-layer count. Controlled live-room acoustics are authored, with unspecified capture hardware and global tuning omitted.

tradition.name: Igbo traditional
tradition.lineage: Complete original Side B band6(a), Ibo Drummers and Dancers, recorded by Stanley Diamond in Owerri Province during1958–59. Issuer liner notes explicitly describe a travelling five-musician orchestra: four musicians play skin-headed drums and one plays a hollow-log slit drum. Drums are precisely tuned and played melodically; caption documents wooden-stick playing and a set of four differently sized skin-covered drums in the pictured subset. Four skin-drum musicians does not mean only four total drums. All five players and both sound families are retained. This is the whole separately documented original6(a) performance, not the adjacent6(b) national celebration or the entire multi-ethnic album. Digital track206 combines both sub-selections; no unverified digital edit timestamp is supplied. A single whole skin-drum-ensemble card retains all four players and their multiple tuned drums; exact individual drum counts, dimensions, tuning frequencies and shell material remain unspecified. It is not replaced with the existing conical hand-played igba. The hollow-log role uses existing Igbo ekwe with authored medium two-tone size and interlocking dance support; size, pitch count and exact timeline are editorial choices, not measured original parameters. The documented instrumental orchestra has zero separately credited singers; incidental crowd sounds are not claimed absent. Authored controlled-room re-recording, no original field-recorder reconstruction, capture apparatus or global tuning claimed. Neutral instrument axes are placeholders, not acoustic measurements.

tradition.lineage: Mafús — complete artist-documented Trujillo quartet practice. Artist own profile explicitly describes the Trujillo Peru group as indie rock/pop rock/pop punk formed2017 and enumerates Rómulo Zavu voice/guitar, Facundo Chejolán drums, Alejandro Koala Salinas guitar and Rafael Fernández bass. The selected scope is that complete explicitly listed quartet practice, not the2018 Nico demo session: the same page credits a different session bassist Cristian Rojas for that recording and does not explicitly name its singer. Two guitarists are aggregated in one guitar-family card, with the one positively named practice singer retained. Trujillo independent-rock city-focused branch, positively anchored by artist indie-rock self-definition and Trujillo formation/profile. Broad Peruvian indie and Latin alternative overlap but are broader geographic umbrellas; no claim every Trujillo musician shares a unique sound. This source directly establishes selected practice and locality without needing invented creator-map membership. Alternative-rock parent is supported by artist independent/alternative-rock labeling. Full named quartet remains; absence of guest credits from a different album does not authorize dropping anything from that album, which is not the selected scope. Authored contemporary electric-guitar realization uses alder/maple humbucker construction and distorted power-chord articulation; bass dual-single-coil fingerstyle and conventional drum kit. These physical choices are representative defaults, not actual documented performer gear. Neutral vocal physiology and source-unspecified articulation; no measured original style claim. Balanced live-room recording and omitted apparatus/global tuning are editorial choices. The actual existing indie_rock_peruano is a national indie-rock umbrella with a representative Lima branch, peruvian_indie spans national indie including acoustic-pop/chamber practice, and pop_peruano is broader national popular-song repertoire. None excludes Trujillo. This requested label is a narrower city-focused indie branch; primary evidence here establishes this band’s regional indie identity, not a separately researched multi-band city network.

tradition.name: Indonesian bamboo
tradition.lineage: Dusun Tanjung senggayung ensemble — Kalait Cambung, complete1998issued field-recorded composition. The Smithsonian-issued complete1:42 Kalait Cambung (SFW40444_107) credits Aron, Atong, Kanal, Karbin, Sehat, Silon, Stephanus Jinar, Tular, Yakobus and Yosep on bamboo tubes. Publisher explicitly marks instrumental. Full field notes identify this and three neighboring tracks as exclusively senggayung bamboo-tube pieces, not the gong/drum ensemble heard on separate tracks2–4. All positively credited sound roles are retained in one family owner. Ten people are credited in the track metadata; field notes describe seven simultaneous paired-tube roles. The evidence preserves this difference rather than inventing how credits were distributed or claiming ten simultaneous parts. The selected complete composition is repeated three times with only minor differences. Indonesian bamboo is a broad material/ensemble discovery field rather than an alias for Java/Bali gamelan or Sundanese shaken angklung. Primary Smithsonian directly documents this Indonesian struck-bamboo repertoire outside those construction and regional practices; secondary exact category mirrors corroborate the named ensemble, while direct creator retrieval failed. Selected Upper Jelai senggayung is exclusively performed in besenggayung fruit-harvest ritual, with memorized homophonic irregular-meter compositions, named register roles and no improvisation. Broad artMusic scopes this formally transmitted fixed tuned repertoire; no concert-purpose or devotional-worship claim is made, and the Southeast Asian layered-ostinato subnode is intentionally not used. Source descriptions specify seven pairs of fresh bamboo tubes with one closed node and cut tongue-like extensions, struck together with differentiated grip muting. Source pitches are approximate; global temperament is omitted rather than pretending exact equal temperament. One aggregate owner preserves the whole named seven-pair configuration, not seven separate electronic notes or playback of a finished recording. Controlled live-room rendition and neutral axes are authored present-day choices, not the original outdoor field-recording environment.

tradition.name: Indonesian experimental
tradition.lineage: Catu Daya — Babat Kawat (2025), complete eight-piece release. Issuer explicitly identifies Catu Daya as Indonesian experimental duo Yustiawan Paradigma Umar and Yoga Nugraha Usmad. Complete release credits name Javanese rebab, gong ageng, electronics and field recordings, all performed by the duo and recorded live at Lokananta in Surakarta. The described practice combines acoustic gamelan resources, environmental material and electronic ambient/drone improvisation. Eight pieces and the complete four-family palette are retained; generic gamelan bio language does not add uncredited metallophones or singers. Indonesian experimental names a cross-medium contemporary experimental practice rather than all Indonesian traditional gamelan or all national electronic dance music. Existing javanese_gamelan describes cyclic court/village ensemble structures, full gamelan resources and wayang contexts; the selected duo instead documents live electronic/environmental transformation and improvisatory spatial engagement. Existing indonesian_electronic overlaps its technology but does not exhaust the wider acoustic/electronic experimental field. This is a narrower overlapping experimental-practice axis, not a claim that national electronic music excludes experimentation. Broad experimentalElec fits the actual electroacoustic process and drone/ambient composition, without assigning a more specific industrial or dance form. Rebab remains the positively named Javanese instrument with chamber context; carved hardwood, goat skin, steel strings and rough sustained drone are authored physical/articulation choices, not measured original gear. The existing generic gong family is deliberately pinned to its bossed pitched-gong variant, preserving the gong ageng mechanism rather than substituting an indefinite-pitch tam-tam; soft mallet is authored and no original diameter/pitch asserted. Neutral credited-electronics owner preserves unknown generator architecture. Environmental-collage owner represents the explicitly credited field-recording layer assembled in the complete mix, not the finished musical master, an invented sampler or a claim that all field material is voice-free. No separately credited live singer is added, while any embedded environmental voices remain unknown. No global tuning is asserted. Controlled live-room capture is an authored rendition, not a measurement of Lokananta geometry.

tradition.name: Iranian experimental
tradition.lineage: Sote — Majestic Noise Made in Beautiful Rotten Iran, complete eight-piece synthesis release. Complete publisher release lists eight pieces and describes an all-electronic synthetic compositional project. In firsthand discussion of this exact album, Sote enumerates FM, physical modeling, additive, subtractive, wavetable, granular and spectral synthesis. All seven methods are retained as one explicitly aggregate generation palette, without substituting a playback of the opaque final master. Acoustic collaborators from different Sote projects and generic early-career found-object/cassette practice are not imported. No separately credited singer is added. Publisher2020 date and March2022 contemporary interview chronology differ; no exact issue-date reconciliation is asserted. Iranian experimental is a cross-medium experimental-arts network. Exact creator map includes Sote, Saba Alizadeh and Crows in the Rain; Sote firsthand describes the Iranian experimental composer community and Zabte Sote platform. Crows in the Rain own store explicitly identifies post-rock/ambient band practice, positively supporting a network beyond electronic composition alone. Existing persian_electronic is a broad overlapping national electronic category, not restricted to its Ash Koosha sampling exemplar; synthetic Sote works legitimately overlap it. The distinction is the wider experimental art/rock/composer community across media, not different nationality labels, dates or one alternative synthesizer. No claim every Iranian experimental artist is electronic. The selected fully synthetic deconstructive-composition branch supports broad experimentalElec. The isolated aggregate owner preserves every positively named synthesis method and intentionally leaves actual hardware/software, physical controllers, detailed algorithms and sequencing protocol unspecified. No added live percussion, acoustic strings or singer is fabricated from symphonic metaphors. Optional global tuning is omitted because composer specifically alters modal and tonal codes. Neutral axes and treated studio are authored rendering coordinates, not a measured room or claims about an analog capture chain.

tradition.name: Irish ballad
tradition.lineage: The Irish Country Four — The Heights of Alma, complete track15 on Topic TSDL209 (1971). Publisher booklet explicitly credits the entire Heights of Alma track to Trevor Stewart and Jess Harpur singing unaccompanied. Its notes identify an1854 Crimean-war narrative circulated as a street ballad especially widely in Ireland. The group is documented in Northern Irish folk-song practice, with Belfast-linked performers and Ulster repertoire. Select this separately complete track, not a reduced full-album reproduction; accompaniment and other singers on the other sixteen selections are not imported. Irish ballad is a narrative-song repertoire category that can be realized by solo singers, duets and accompanied folk groups. Existing traditional_irish_singing explicitly models solo unaccompanied English-language practice; existing sean_nos_solo models Irish-Gaelic ornamented solo tradition. Both overlap this wider narrative repertoire but do not exhaust its ensemble/accompanied forms. The selected publisher positively documents an unaccompanied two-singer version, not just a different solo performer. Existing irish_rebel_song is a political/rebellion subset; a Crimean-war historical street ballad is not automatically Irish rebellion. Existing celtic_irish_trad foregrounds instrumental dance sessions rather than complete narrative song. No claim all Irish ballads exclude those categories or originate exclusively in Ireland: the booklet explicitly traces English, Scottish and Irish circulation. Celtic balladic parent fits the positively described narrative oral/broadside repertoire. Two positively named singers use an authored combined live duet with source-unspecified physiology, pitch system and articulation; exact original take or overdub count not asserted. Controlled live-room capture and omitted apparatus/global tuning are editorial choices, not claimed1971 studio facts.

tradition.name: Japanese instrumental
tradition.lineage: Kazumi Tateishi Trio — complete documented Ghibli-meets-jazz piano-trio practice. The label’s complete named trio profile credits Kazumi Tateishi piano/arranging, Shinobu Sato bass, Mao Suzuki drums. The organizer’s full artist introduction on Seoul City’s culture portal explicitly identifies Sato’s instrument as double bass and describes the trio’s established Ghibli jazz-arrangement/improvisation practice. All three musicians and three instrument families are retained, with no singer. This models the documented complete ensemble practice, not a claim to have inspected every2010album session credit or witnessed the future December2026 concert. The original label album page positively describes swinging and funky jazz arrangements of Ghibli melodies. Japanese instrumental is a cross-instrument and cross-repertoire wordless listening/discovery field. The exact linked creator playlist freshly reproduced by the independent reviewer (turn702452view0, first100 positions) spans piano, guitar, harp and music-box providers, supporting a cross-instrument field rather than existing japanese_piano or japanese_guitar alone. An earlier author observation of the full creator map (turn762587view0) included Kazumi Tateishi Trio and AUN J-Classic Orchestra, but this precise membership could not be independently reproduced after map retrieval failures; no retained successful raw response is claimed. The selected trio is independently documented Japanese instrumental practice, without relying on that unbound membership observation. AUN’s own primary description separately documents wadaiko/shamisen/koto/shakuhachi/shinobue/narimono and accessible new compositions, corroborating Japanese cross-instrument practice only, not freshly verified creator membership. Existing japanese_jazz and jazz_cover overlap this selected trio branch but do not exhaust the cross-style Japanese instrumental network. No national sound-exclusive claim and no equation of all Japanese music with this discovery field. Jazz parent applies only to the explicit improvising trio realization, not the entire field. Authored modern nine-foot Steinway D, jazz-chordal piano touch, steel-string upright double bass in pizzicato, and conventional jazz brush-kit are coherent contemporary choices rather than measured source construction or exact arrangement. The existing Upright (double) bass owner explicitly models plucked jazz bass without importing orchestral bowing apparatus. Controlled live-room recording and absent global tuning/apparatus are editorial choices.

tradition.name: Japanese prog
tradition.lineage: RUINZHATOVA — Live in Somewhere, complete six-piece release (original2006; digital2020). The artist-run Magaibutsu/Ruins release describes Japanese progressive/experimental musicians and complete improvised free-rock performances; six pieces are listed. Its full personnel credits retain Yamamoto Seiichi guitar, Tsuyama Atsushi bass (credited Tsuyana on the page) and Yoshida Tatsuya drums. No singer is credited; the authored palette follows this complete three-instrument credit sheet rather than assuming uncredited vocals or synthesizers. The June2020 digital release explicitly identifies original January2006 issue. Japanese prog is a national progressive/experimental-rock network: the creator map includes Ruins, KENSO, Ars Nova, Koenjihyakkei, Sadistic Mika Band and Acoustic Asturias. The selected Ruinzhatova collaboration is on the Ruins artist-run release page and explicitly described as Japanese progressive free-rock; it is not asserted to be a separate creator-map member. Existing progressive_rock describes the classic UK-rooted composition-centered tradition and later revival, whereas this national network encompasses a documented free-improvising branch. Existing zeuhl and zeuhl_french legitimately include Japanese followers; Japanese prog is not equivalent to that narrower Magma-derived Kobaian/ostinato lineage. Existing japanese_psychedelic_rock and japanoise overlap artists but describe respectively psychedelic repetition/fuzz and saturated noise practice, not the whole documented progressive network. This is an overlapping regional umbrella, not a claim all Japanese progressive music has one distinct sound. Broad experimental-rock parent is limited to the selected extended free-rock improvisation rather than asserting composed classical suites. Authored rendition uses an alder/maple humbucker guitar with overdriven single-note lead, compatible alder/maple dual-single-coil fingerstyle bass, and conventional rock kit. Actual performer materials, amps, meter and recording apparatus are not documented and are not claimed. Controlled live-room capture and omitted global tuning/apparatus are editorial choices.

The Latin Recording Academy separately recognizes Christian albums in Spanish, and Witt’s own CanZion Christian music school publishes this exact devotional song. This is an observed community concentration, not a claim every member is Catholic or all repertoire disjoint. Latin Christian’s independently documented Spanish Christian commercial/ministry field spans additional gospel, rap, rock and worship networks; exact broad creator roster names Witt, Redimi2 and Miel San Marcos. tradition.name: Malayalam worship
tradition.lineage: The Twelve — complete 2019 a cappella devotional-film-song medley issued by Pilgrims Communications. All eight human voices are represented by one ensemble voice card: four song singers and four vocal accompanists, not eight independently notated counterpoint parts. Authored live-group rendition with unspecified voicing and neutral source-unspecified physiology preserves the source roles without claiming measured overdub count, SATB registers, beatboxing anatomy or exact original vocal effects. No instruments, tuning system or capture apparatus are invented. Controlled live room and unprocessed present-day voices are authored realization choices, not a reconstruction of the source recording.

extras.description: First-person interview with band member Fr Eby Edassery names four song vocalists and four human voices supplying the orchestral accompaniment. It explicitly describes the instrumental-free a cappella practice and the complete medley of four Malayalam devotional film songs, issued by the Ernakulam-Angamaly archdiocesan media ministry. All eight named contributors are retained; the name The Twelve does not imply twelve performers.
